title: poc-sandboxing-and-data-paths-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a playbook for running a retail customer POC that needs rapid iteration on features while proving production-grade controls for PII and latency-sensitive inference. The core idea: use a sandbox-first pattern that explicitly maps data paths across three deployment tiers (hosted dev, dedicated staging, private prod) and prescribes controls / runbooks for moving artifacts between them.

Context / customer summary:
- Customer: mid-market retail analytics platform (approx. 120 engineers, global ops).
- POC ask: conversational product recommender + session-level personalization. Data contains hashed user ids, PII in logs, and some EU-resident customers.
- Success metrics requested: 95th percentile inference latency < 220ms (interactive), model correctness (NDCG@10 uplift >= 6%), and evidence of a secure data path for EU traffic.

Constraints and non-negotiables:
- No raw PII leaves customer environment in prod.
- They want sub-week feature turnaround in POC dev iterations.
- Budget capped for POC at ~ $20k desktop-equivalent compute for 8 weeks.
- Must produce an ops playbook to hand to their SREs before any final migration.

High-level sandbox pattern (three-tier mapping):
1) Hosted (Dev sandbox) - fast iteration
   - Redwood hosted inference (standard API) with synthetic or strongly redacted datasets.
   - Use feature flags and redaction proxy to remove PII before hitting Redwood hosted endpoints.
   - Accepts small traffic from internal testers only.
2) Dedicated (Staging sandbox) - performance validation
   - Reserved Dedicated capacity in a region close to customer staging cluster.
   - Ingest de-identified production-like samples (token counts, session lengths) via secure transfer.
   - Run load tests, latency p95 measurements, and real-value evals (NDCG, CTR sim).
   - Canary fallback configured to Hosted variant for scale tests.
3) Private (Production gate) - data sovereignty and final security
   - Private deployment inside customer VPC / on-prem package if required by compliance.
   - Raw PII stays in customer's environment; only model weights and telemetry aggregates leave.
   - Tight network policies and KMS integration (customer-managed keys).

Novel recommendation (sandbox data-paths matrix):
- Treat every artifact as 3-tuples: {prompt_templates, eval_prompts, telemetry_keyset}. For each tuple define allowed movement rules and obfuscation levels.
- Use a stable mapping table (versioned CSV) that lists which prompt/eval files are allowed to cross tiers and what transformation is required (hash, redact, synthetic augmentation).
- Automate the mapping via a small CLI (poc-tool) that enforces transformation rules before upload. (See linked GH PR for prototype.)

Tradeoffs (why this pattern):
- Pros: fast dev loop in hosted environment, realistic perf validation on Dedicated, and strict data control at Private. Clear handoff boundaries reduce surprises at final deployment.
- Cons: extra engineering to maintain transformers and mapping, potential double-testing overhead, and added orchestration of rollouts.

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
Phase 0: Kickoff + baseline
- Identify data steward and SRE points of contact on customer side.
- Baseline: collect session length histogram, token distribution, and common prompt templates (anonymized).
- Deliverable: POC intake doc (JIRA-SEA-789).

Phase 1: Hosted dev sandbox (days 1–7)
- Wire up redaction proxy in front of Redwood hosted API.
- Load synthetic data and smoke-test the recommender.
- Quick eval: smoke NDCG on small probe set.
- Checkpoints: onboarding call, security checklist sign-off.

Phase 2: Dedicated staging (days 8–28)
- Provision Dedicated pool sized for expected concurrency (estimate: 8 GPUs for p99 target under 500 QPS internal sim) — see capacity notes below.
- Run progressive load tests: 10k requests -> 50k -> production-simulated peak.
- Validate latency SLO, billing telemetry, and cache-hit rates.
- Run adversarial prompt suite (security eval).

Phase 3: Private gating (days 29–56)
- Deliver runbook for customer SREs to deploy the on-prem or VPC package.
- Integrate KMS and audit logging; verify no raw PII leaves network.
- Conduct failover tests: simulate Dedicated outage and verify graceful fallback to hosted (if allowed by policy).

Capacity and rough cost guidance (POC window):
- Hosted dev: minimal cost (metered). Budget ~$1k total for experimentation.
- Dedicated staging: reserve small GPU slab for 4 weeks, estimate $8–12k depending on instance types and region. We propose using mixed-precision quantized variants for cost savings during load testing.
- Private: customer bears infra cost; Redwood support hours estimated 40h for integration during POC (T-shirt $10k professional services).

Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
- End-to-end flow: sample session processed from customer ingestion to personalized recommendation with telemetry in Console.
- Performance: P95 latency < 220ms in Dedicated under target load; no functional regressions vs baseline.
- Security: signed attestation that raw PII never left private environment for prod gating; KMS integrated.
- Observability: traces and token-cost breakdown visible in Redwood Console for at least 30 days of synthetic traffic.

Engineering runbook (commands & artifacts) - quick list:
- poc-tool transform --input prompts/ --rules mapping.csv --output /tmp/clean_prompts
- deploy-dedicated --profile retail-staging --pool-size 8 --image v2.1-quant
- run-loadtest --target staging.redwood.customer --qps 400 --duration 30m
- smoke-eval --goldset evals/retail_goldset.json --endpoint {dedicated}

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: customer data leakage during staging ingestion. Mitigation: require SFTP + PGP-signed transfers + activate audit logging and ephemeral storage that wipes after ingestion.
- Risk: insufficient Dedicated capacity leads to missed SLO during ramp. Mitigation: pre-reserve burstable nodes and test fallback routing.
- Risk: eval mismatch between hosted redacted data and real prod distribution. Mitigation: enforce a small-scale shadow run in customer environment for real traces (synthetic labels) before prod cutover.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self style):
- Confirm legal review timeline for EU data flow (who owns this? legal@customer).
- Finalize mapping.csv rules for email/phone; current rules are conservative (drop token ranges). Need product input on acceptability for model prompt context.
- Check availability of region-bound Dedicated capacity for week-of-Nov-11. (Arjun to ping infra capacity team.)

Customer handoff deliverables:
- Ops runbook (this doc + stepwise commands)
- Mini-conformance checklist for SREs
- Synthetic-to-real trace comparison report

Appendix: quick eval checklist (copy into ticket)
- Dataset: 10k anonymized sessions or equivalent synthetic set
- Metrics to capture: latency p50/p95/p99, tokens-per-request distribution, model confidence distribution, NDCG@10 vs baseline
- Smoke tests: 20 manual queries covering edge cases + 1000 synthetic emulation

Notes:
- This playbook is intentionally light-weight; for enterprise POC expand the security gating and add SIEM integration tasks.
- Prototype CLI and mapping.csv are in the linked GH PR; consider wrapping as a small npm package for future POCs.
